title: Sigma/pi, hybridisation and resonance; formal charge; Carbocation stability and Markovnikov
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BD07#t3 term and clue written for the game; BD07#t4 term and clue written for the game; BD07#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR13#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD07#N.5, OR13#N.3, BD07#N.13, OR13#N.6, OR13#N.8b, OR13#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Free rotation
items.clue: Groups can turn about a single C–C link, but not about C=C.

items.label: Trigonal planar
items.clue: Arrangement around each C of C=C: three bonding regions at about 120°.

items.label: Pi bond
items.clue: Sideways overlap of two p orbitals, with electron density above and below the axis.

items.label: Tertiary carbocation
items.clue: The most stable type of C⁺ species, with three alkyl groups bonded to the charged atom.

questions.stem: A student suggests that a π bond between two carbon atoms prevents rotation about the bond that joins them. Which observation does this hypothesis predict?

options.text: ClHC=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClH₂C–CH₂Cl exists as two separable compounds
H₂C=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClC≡CCl exists as two separable compounds

questions.explanation: With no rotation, the two Cl atoms are fixed on the same side or opposite sides of C=C: two isomers. ClH₂C–CH₂Cl has no π bond, so it rotates and is one compound.

questions.stem: Which carbocation is the most stable?

options.text: CH₃⁺
CH₃CH₂CH₂⁺
CH₃CH⁺CH₃
(CH₃)₃C⁺

questions.explanation: This is tertiary: three alkyl groups on the positive carbon. Tertiary carbocations are the most stable.

questions.stem: Mean (average) bond enthalpies: C–C 347 kJ mol⁻¹ · C=C 612 kJ mol⁻¹ · C≡C 838 kJ mol⁻¹. A C≡C bond is only about 2.4 times as strong as a C–C bond, not 3 times. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its three shared pairs repel one another, so C≡C is longer than C–C.
All three of its bonds are σ bonds, but they are weaker because they share space.
Two of its three bonds come from sideways overlap of p orbitals, which is less effective.
Its π electrons lie on the axis between the nuclei, where σ electrons repel them.

questions.explanation: C≡C is one σ and two π. Each π adds less than a σ: 612 − 347 = 265, then 838 − 612 = 226. So the total is well below 3 × 347 = 1041.

questions.stem: 2-methylbut-1-ene, CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃, reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the major product, and why?

options.text: 1-bromo-2-methylbutane, as it forms via a tertiary carbocation
2-bromo-2-methylbutane, as it forms via a tertiary carbocation
2-bromo-2-methylbutane, as Br adds to the carbon that has more H atoms
1-bromo-2-methylbutane, as the primary carbocation is less crowded, so it forms faster

questions.explanation: H adds to the CH₂ end (C1). The C⁺ on C2 has three alkyl groups: tertiary, the most stable. Br⁻ bonds to it: CH₃CBr(CH₃)CH₂CH₃.

questions.stem: 2-methylpropene, (CH₃)₂C=CH₂, reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the minor product, and which carbocation does it form through?

options.text: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, via a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylpropane, via a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylpropane, via a primary carbocation
1,2-dibromo-2-methylpropane, via a secondary carbocation

questions.explanation: If H adds to the central carbon, C⁺ is on the CH₂ end: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂⁺, primary. This slow route gives the minor product, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br.

questions.stem: 1-methylcyclohexene is a six-membered ring with one C=C. One C=C carbon carries a CH₃ group and no H; the other carries one H. It reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the major product, and why?

options.text: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane, as H adds to the CH carbon of the C=C, giving a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane, as H adds to the carbon carrying the CH₃ group, giving a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane, as Br goes to the carbon with more space around it
Equal amounts of both, as the ring makes both carbons of the C=C equivalent

questions.explanation: With H on the CH carbon, C⁺ is on the ring carbon bearing CH₃: three alkyl groups, tertiary. Br⁻ bonds there, so Br and CH₃ share a carbon.
